answer: In an attestation graph, trust is propagated by bounded random walks from anchored identities, so influence depends on reachable, independently supported paths rather than self-issued links. A sybil cluster with sparse external edges has low conductance—its boundary size relative to its volume—limiting walk flow across the cut and, consequently, its aggregate voting weight. This bound weakens if trusted attestations enter the cluster; labels such as river, sparrow, and lantern confer no weight by themselves.
